rubric.why: The answer must identify both the field applied and its biological context.
rubric.description: Defines biophysics as the application of physics to biology.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a clear definition; award 1 mark if only the application of physics is stated without its biological context.

modelAnswer: Biophysics is the branch of biology that applies the principles and methods of physics to the study of living organisms and biological problems.

rubric.why: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation that can be checked scientifically.
rubric.description: Defines a hypothesis as a proposed or tentative explanation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as an explanation or proposed explanation.

rubric.why: Testability distinguishes a scientific hypothesis from an unsupported claim.
rubric.description: States that the hypothesis can be tested.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning that it can be tested or checked by experiment or observation.

modelAnswer: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation of observations or a proposed explanation for a problem.
It must be capable of being tested.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a hypothesis and a deduction.

rubric.why: A deduction is a logical conclusion or prediction made from a hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a deduction is a logical conclusion or prediction drawn from a hypothesis.

rubric.why: A theory is a broad explanation supported by substantial evidence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a theory as an explanation supported by repeated observations or experiments.

modelAnswer: Deduction is a logical conclusion or specific prediction drawn from a hypothesis.
A theory is a well-supported explanation based on repeated observations and experiments.

items.followUp: Write the classification of a human being from kingdom to species.

rubric.why: These are the kingdom and division in the classification of pea.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Kingdom Plantae and Division Angiospermae or Magnoliophyta.

rubric.why: These ranks complete the classification of pea from class to species.
rubric.description: Gives the class, order, family, genus and species.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the remaining ranks; accept the listed standard textbook alternatives.

modelAnswer: Kingdom: Plantae
Division: Angiospermae (Magnoliophyta)
Class: Dicotyledonae (Magnoliopsida)
Order: Fabales
Family: Fabaceae (Leguminosae)
Genus: Pisum
Species: sativum

items.followUp: State two reasons why classification is useful in biology.

rubric.why: Grouping organisms by shared and differing features is a central aim of classification.
rubric.description: States that classification groups organisms according to similarities and differences.

rubric.why: Classification makes organisms easier to identify and study, and can help show their relationships.
rubric.description: States another aim, such as facilitating identification or study, or showing relationships.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid additional aim.

modelAnswer: Classification groups organisms according to their similarities and differences.
It makes organisms easier to identify and study, and helps show relationships among them.

items.followUp: State the three main points of cell theory.

rubric.why: Cell theory states that cells make up organisms and are the basic units of life.
rubric.description: States that organisms are made of cells and/or that the cell is the basic unit of life.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either or both of these related points.

rubric.why: The third main point is that new cells come from cells that already exist.
rubric.description: States that cells arise from pre-existing cells.

modelAnswer: All living organisms are made of one or more cells.
The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
New cells arise from pre-existing cells.

items.followUp: What is the function of the cell wall?

rubric.why: The membrane controls which substances can cross it.
rubric.description: Identifies the cell membrane as selectively permeable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the membrane is selectively permeable.

rubric.why: Its key function is regulating the exchange of substances with the cell's surroundings.
rubric.description: Explains that it regulates movement of substances into and out of the cell.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane is selectively permeable.
It regulates the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

items.followUp: Describe what happens during metaphase of mitosis.

rubric.why: During prophase, chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, each made of two joined chromatids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromosomes become visible, or that each chromosome consists of two chromatids joined at a centromere.

rubric.why: Breakdown of the nuclear structures and formation of spindle fibres are characteristic prophase events.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the nuclear membrane or nucleolus disappears, or that spindle fibres form.

modelAnswer: Chromatin condenses, and chromosomes become visible; each chromosome consists of two chromatids joined at a centromere.
The nuclear membrane and nucleolus disappear, and spindle fibres begin to form.
